
---
title: "Data Cleaning"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Loading the Data

First, we load the dataset that we will use for our project.

```{r}
# Load the original World Bank dataset
data <- read.csv("WB_WDI_SE_XPD_TOTL_GD_ZS_WIDEF.csv")

# Check the original data
dim(data)
summary(data$X2020)

# Create cleaned dataset
clean_data <- data

# Remove duplicate rows
clean_data <- unique(clean_data)

# Check available observations for 2020
sum(!is.na(clean_data$X2020))

# Save cleaned dataset
save(clean_data, file = "12_DataSaving.RData")
```

## Checking for Missing Values

We check if there are any missing values in our dataset.

```{r}
# Count missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(data))

# Check the number of rows and columns
dim(data)
```

## Removing Missing Values

We remove rows with missing values so they do not affect our analysis.

```{r}
# Remove rows with missing values
clean_data <- na.omit(data)

# Check the new dimensions
dim(clean_data)
```

## Checking for Duplicates

Next, we check for duplicate rows and remove them if needed.

```{r}
# Count duplicate rows
sum(duplicated(clean_data))

# Remove duplicates
clean_data <- unique(clean_data)
```

## Checking Variable Types

We check the types of variables to make sure the data is in the correct format.

```{r}
# Look at the structure of cleaned data
str(clean_data)

# Summary of the cleaned data
summary(clean_data)
```

## Saving the Cleaned Data

Finally, we save the cleaned dataset so we can use it for the next part of our analysis.

```{r}
# Save cleaned data
save(clean_data, file = "12_DataSaving.RData")
```
